title: Pesapunck
summary: Pesapunck is a Southold placename for a neck and meadow between Cutchogue and Mattituck, interpreted as a hot house or sweat lodge place.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern farmland/shoreline point between Cutchogue and Mattituck near Peconic Bay, used as a general proxy for Pesapunck; exact neck, meadow, and Deep Hole location need local map review.
why_this_matters: Translating to "hothouse," the Algonquian place name Pesapunck identifies the precise historic location of a traditional domed sweat lodge built into the side of a local hill or brook for intense physical and spiritual cleansing. Because modern Long Island Indigenous communities continue to actively utilize sweat lodges today, reclaiming this long-standing geographic name highlights a powerful, unbroken continuity of Native spiritual practices.
introduction_content: Pesapunck names a neck and meadow in Southold town between Cutchogue and Mattituck, a landscape remembered in both place-name research and local site history.
history_content: Pesapunck belongs to a Peconic Bay farm, meadow, and creek-edge landscape between Corchaug/Cutchogue and Mattituck. Landholding and spelling details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
Related forms include Pissapunke, Pissapunck, Pessepunk, Pesapunch, Pisapunke, and Pieceapunck. The name is interpreted as a hot house or sweat lodge place.

Why Place Names Matter

“The Other 250 maps the place-names that hold what the official story leaves out — and the movements working to remember, reclaim, and repair.”

— The Other 250 project team, The Other 250 (2026), Project introduction
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point between Cutchogue and Mattituck near Peconic Bay. This marker is not an exact neck, meadow, sweat lodge, or archaeological-site coordinate.
